exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Planning a Wildlife Trip
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Where do you want to go this weekend, Tom?
Tom: I'd love to visit the national park to watch wild birds.
Lily: That sounds great. What do you hope to see there?
Tom: Mostly eagles. I really want to take a photo of one flying.
Lily: Then we should get up very early in the morning.
Tom: Yes, dawn is the time when most birds are active.
Lily: Good idea. I'll bring my camera too.
Tom: Perfect. Remember to stay quiet so we don't frighten them away.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 问 Tom 周末想去哪;Tom 想去国家公园观野鸟,主要想拍飞翔的鹰;两人决定清晨早起,因为黎明时鸟最活跃;Lily 也带相机;Tom 提醒要保持安静,以免吓跑鸟。

questions.stem: Where does Tom want to go this weekend?
What does Tom mainly hope to see?
Why do they decide to get up early?
options: Because most birds are active at dawn.
Because the park closes at noon.

questions.stem: What will Lily bring along?
What does Tom remind Lily to do?
options: Stay quiet so they do not frighten the birds.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Why Animals Travel
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many animals do not spend the whole year in one place.
When food runs low in winter, they move to warmer areas.
Some travel a long way to find a safe place for their young.
Birds, fish and even some insects make these yearly journeys.
The trips are full of danger, but they help the animals live on.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多动物并非整年待在一个地方;冬天食物变少时,它们迁往温暖地区;有些长途跋涉为幼崽寻找安全之地;鸟、鱼甚至一些昆虫都进行这样的年度旅程;旅途充满危险,但帮助动物生存下去。

questions.stem: What do many animals NOT do?
options: Spend the whole year in one place.

questions.stem: Why do animals move when winter comes?
Why do some animals travel a long way?
options: To find a safe place for their young.

questions.stem: Which animals make these yearly journeys?
options: Birds, fish and even some insects.

questions.stem: What do these dangerous trips help animals do?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 The Zoo Debate
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: I think zoos are good because they protect animals in danger.
Jack: But a zoo can never give an animal its real home in the wild.
Mia: That's true, yet zoos help children learn about animals.
Jack: They can learn from films and books instead.
Mia: Still, seeing a real tiger is not the same as watching a film.
Jack: I agree it's exciting, but I worry the animals are not free.
Mia: So you think zoos are built more for people than for animals?
Jack: Exactly. That's my biggest reason for being against them.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 认为动物园好,因为能保护濒危动物;Jack 认为动物园永远给不了动物真正的野外家园;Mia 说动物园能让孩子了解动物;Jack 说看影片和书也能学;Mia 说亲眼看真老虎和看影片不一样;Jack 担心动物不自由,认为动物园更多是为人而建——这是他反对的最大理由。

questions.stem: Why does Mia think zoos are good?
options: They make a lot of money.

questions.stem: What is Jack's first point against zoos?
options: A zoo cannot give an animal its real wild home.

questions.stem: How does Mia reply when Jack mentions films and books?
options: She says seeing a real tiger is not the same as a film.

questions.stem: What does Jack worry about?
options: That the animals are not free.

questions.stem: What is Jack's biggest reason for being against zoos?
options: He believes zoos are built more for people than for animals.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The Monarch Butterfly
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Each autumn, monarch butterflies fly thousands of kilometres south.
For years, no one knew how they found the right way.
Scientists learned that the insect uses the sun to guide it.
Sadly, the number of monarchs has dropped very fast.
People are now working together to help them survive.
exercises.translation_cn: 每年秋天,黑脉金斑蝶向南飞行数千公里;多年来无人知道它们如何找到正确方向;科学家发现这种昆虫靠太阳指引;遗憾的是,金斑蝶数量下降得很快;如今人们正合力帮助它们生存。

questions.stem: When do the monarch butterflies fly south?
What did people NOT know for years?
options: How the butterflies found the right way.

questions.stem: What guides the butterfly, according to scientists?
What has happened to the number of monarchs?
What are people doing now?
options: Working together to help them survive.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Advice for Watching Bears
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Ben: I'm going to photograph bears next week. Any advice?
Sara: Yes. Never get too close to a wild bear.
Ben: How close is too close?
Sara: Keep at least a hundred metres away to stay safe.
Ben: What if a bear suddenly looks at me?
Sara: Stay calm, don't run, and move back slowly.
Ben: That's good to know. Anything else?
Sara: Yes, always respect the animal. We are visitors in its world.
exercises.translation_cn: Ben 下周要拍熊,向 Sara 求建议;Sara 说绝不要太靠近野熊,至少保持一百米;若熊忽然看着你,要保持冷静、别跑、慢慢后退;最后她说要永远尊重动物,我们是它世界里的客人。

questions.stem: What is Ben going to do next week?
What is Sara's first piece of advice?
options: Never get too close to a wild bear.

questions.stem: How far away should Ben stay to be safe?
What should Ben do if a bear looks at him?
options: Stay calm and move back slowly.

questions.stem: What does Sara say at the end?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Respecting Wild Animals
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Wild animals are not pets, and they belong in nature.
When we visit their world, we should be quiet and careful.
We must never leave rubbish that could harm them.
Cutting down their forests takes away the homes they need.
If we respect them, both animals and people can live well.
exercises.translation_cn: 野生动物不是宠物,它们属于大自然;当我们进入它们的世界时,应保持安静和小心;绝不能留下可能伤害它们的垃圾;砍伐森林会夺走它们所需的家园;如果我们尊重它们,动物和人都能生活得很好。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about wild animals?
options: They are not pets and belong in nature.

questions.stem: How should we behave when visiting their world?
What must we never leave behind?
What does cutting down forests do?
options: It takes away the homes they need.

questions.stem: What happens if we respect wild animals?
options: Both animals and people can live well.
